sections.text: इति क्षेत्रं तथा ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं चोक्तं समासतः।
Thus I have told thee in brief what Matter is, and the Self worth realising and what is Wisdom. He who is devoted to Me knows; and assuredly he will enter into Me.
Know thou further that Nature and God have no beginning; and that differences of character and quality have their origin in Nature only.
Nature is the Law which generates cause and effect; God is the source of the enjoyment of all pleasure and pain.

We have seen in this chapter that in verse number three, Bhagavan has given us a formula for liberation. He basically says that knowledge of the field plus the knowledge of the knower of the field equals knowledge of the Supreme Self. To find this enlightenment, Bhagavan said you need to know both -- the field of experiences and the experiencer. In the same verse, he told us that the Kshetrajna is only one. I am the Supreme Lord, the experiencer in all the fields. I am the knower in all the fields. As we have discussed before, the consciousness is one and all-pervading, but it manifests through the equipment which we call body, mind, and intellect.
We feel that this consciousness is within me. But in the last few verses, Bhagavan has described that consciousness as all-pervading. I feel it is within me because it is within and without all things and beings. All things and beings are in the consciousness, but we feel the consciousness is within me. Very similar to our analogy of space -- we think the space is in the room, but actually the room is in the space. We have been given a detailed explanation about the Kshetra.
So we have seen the definition of Kshetra from verse 6 to 7. What is the field of experience? It says this body is the field, which includes the five great elements, all the way up to the modifications of mind, up to fortitude, the dhriti. So everything that I consider as part of my world is included in the field of experiences. And then from verse 8 through 12, Bhagavan has described qualities to be developed, starting from humility, Amanitvam, ending with Tattvajnana-artha-darshanam -- the goal of knowing the knower of the field. What is the purpose of having this knowledge that Bhagavan has described?
And these qualities are the means to achieve the knowledge. So Bhagavan called developing these qualities or having these qualities knowledge. Anything other than that is ignorance. The opposite of all those qualities is ignorance. All these things are limiting me -- this showing off, this high opinion about myself.
Because of that, when I hurt other people knowingly or unknowingly, thats the expression of ignorance. So anything other than these 20 qualities, Bhagavan called it ignorance. And then Bhagavan has described what is to be known in very contradictory terms. Starting from verse 13: Anadi mat-param Brahma. That Brahman which needs to be known is beginningless, and na sat tan nasat ucyate -- it is neither being (sat) nor non-being (asat).
It is also not nothing. So in this contradictory terms, Bhagavan has been explaining the nature of the supreme Brahman that is to be known. That is the goal of knowledge. We came to the last verse we have discussed. We say Bahihi anthasch bhutana _part _part evacha. That supreme Being is within and without all beings.
It is easier for us to think that he is within me and within all the sentient beings. Very, very difficult for me to imagine that he is also outside of me. It appears to be within me, but actually my equipment is within this supreme conscious. Space seems to be within the room defined by its conditionings, four walls, ceiling and floor. But actually space was always here and it will always remain here. Even when you remove this conditionings.
Even though this equipment I call myself as identified with the body, mind and intellect. It seems it is the container for this consciousness. But once it is actually within the consciousness, _part _part evacha. So it is not just limited to the beings. Also things which are achara within a pot and also is outside the pot. But however, I have no experience of this.
So Bhagavan says it is because suksma twat on vignam. It is so subtle that it is not easy to know. So things which are within the capabilities of my senses, I can perceive them. So I can see the visible light. Light is the form of an electromagnetic wave. But within the capabilities of my eyes I can see the visible light.
But any other electromagnetic wave beyond that, Im not capable of seeing them. Radio waves are all over in this room, but Im not capable of detecting them. But the right equipment, it can be detected because they are so subtle that my senses are not capable of grasping them. That does not mean they do not exist. It is very overwhelming for me to even think that consciousness is everywhere. Therefore it is too far for me that is also very close to those who understand its very nature. So one who understands its very nature and experience, for him it is so close because it cannot be any further than my own self. How far I am from my own self, there is no distance to be measured there. I am who I am, where I am. If that I am is the same as the supreme Consciousness, if that understanding takes place, Bhagavan said, very, very close to you.
It is far for the people who have not understood its real nature, but very close to the people who understood its nature. Bhagavan continues in the next verse and says, Vibhaktam Ivachasthitam Even though it is indivisible, it is undivided, ever present, all pervading. It also remains in people as divided selves. So it is something similar to the space we have discussed. Even though the space is indivisible, space cannot be divided, cannot be cut, cannot be separated, cannot be made into pieces. But I feel it is divided among all the rooms and buildings and huts and whatever the type of containers that I can imagine in this world.
So space is divided into small box, big box, small house, big house. However, its very nature is indivisible. So these days, repurposing the old building is a big trend. Because as we, as we call the greenest building is the one which is not built. The second greenest building is one which is repurposed, which is existing. When you repurpose the building, its always old, really messy.
But if you are trained in that profession, then you will visualize the space without all the distractions you have from the existing walls and floors and ceilings. Then you figure out that if I can combine all this space and repurpose it, I can make it useful for whatever the purpose. We are using this building because the space is always indivisible. It is I as the architect who put those divisions in it. So Bhagavan seat for all the people who feel that the concept within them, he remains as the knower within them, but he remains same for everyone. Aviv Bhaktam never gets divided, never gets polluted, never gets chained never gets affected by all the qualities of all those things and beings.
But he remains as he is, but appears to be divided in beings. Bhuta Bhartrucha Tatgneam Bhuta Bharat Rahu is the supporter of all. When I exist in my present state, he is a supporter of my existence. I exist because Im conscious. My consciousness is the supporter of my existence with Bhuta Bhartra. So the same supreme being which is no qualities, neither Sat nor Asat.

Well talk about the knowledge and what is to be known. I explained to you what the _part is. So explained what _part? _part is the one which pervades everywhere. But it seems like divided into all things and beings. Also explained to _part what is knowledge?
Knowledge that enables me to know the supreme self is the knowledge. Therefore we have seen those 20 qualities from Amanitvam to Tatvagnan Orthodarsanam and also explain to you what is to be known. My devotees knowing these will come to my being. As we have said in the beginning Bhagavan has given this formula the knowledge of the field plus the knowledge of the knower of the field equals to the knowledge of the supreme Self. But once now I told you what is the goal? The goal is to know the Supreme Self and the formula is to know the _part and also know the who is the knower of _part?
What is my field of experiences and who is the experiencer? Once you have understood both then you are my _part that you have dissolved your individuality in that supreme self. So mad _part, the one who has surrendered his individuality, one who has surrendered his sense of agency. Once I realized that _part in me I considered to be my ego. So when I considered my consciousness, I am the knower of my experiences, the experiencer, the perceiver, feeler, thinker actually refer to my ego.

Krishna now reveals the relationship between Prakriti (Nature) and Purusha (Spirit): both are beginningless (anadi). All modifications (vikaras) and qualities (gunas) arise from Prakriti alone. Prakriti is the cause of all action through body and senses (karya-karana-kartritva), while Purusha is the cause of experiencing pleasure and pain (sukha-duhkhanam bhoktritva). This is a crucial discrimination: your body acts, your mind thinks, your senses perceive - all this is Prakriti at work. But the sense of I am experiencing this - that witnessing presence - is Purusha.
Reflect on this division of labor in your own experience. When your hand moves, it is Prakriti moving. When your mind worries, it is Prakriti worrying. But the awareness that knows my hand is moving or my mind is worrying - that is the Purusha principle. The Purusha never acts; it only witnesses. Today, notice how naturally you attribute actions to yourself: I am walking, I am thinking, I am feeling. Can you shift to recognizing: Walking is happening and I am aware of it, Thinking is happening and I am aware of it?
The practical implication is liberating: if you are not the doer, you need not carry the burden of doership. Your body-mind will continue to act according to its nature and karma, but you - as awareness - can witness without being crushed by the weight of endless doing. This is not passivity or irresponsibility; it is acting from clarity rather than compulsion. As an exercise, perform one routine task today with full attention but with the inner attitude: Prakriti is doing this; I am the witnessing presence.
